claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy composition.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a fine, uniform dual-phase lamellar fcc/BCC microstructure.
The second phase in baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can be described simply as BCC.
Baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 retains a combination of high tensile strength and ductility up to approximately 700 °C.
The lamellar duplex architecture contributes to the favorable strength–ductility synergy of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The lamellar microstructure is key to environmental or corrosion resistance in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The lamellar microstructure is key to radiation tolerance in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The lamellar microstructure is key to cryogenic toughness in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Increasing Al content beyond the eutectic baseline increases lattice-distortion energy.
Increasing Al content beyond the eutectic baseline effectively lowers configurational-entropy stabilization.
Lattice distortion and configurational entropy mediate the stability of the dual-phase lamellar structure.
Above a critical Al concentration, the balance between fcc and BCC phases is disrupted.
Al contents above the critical concentration reduce lamellar uniformity or promote undesirable secondary phases.
The Al-induced phase and morphology changes degrade high-temperature tensile strength and ductility relative to eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The Al-induced phase and morphology changes reduce corrosion resistance relative to eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The Al-induced phase and morphology changes reduce radiation tolerance relative to eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The Al-induced phase and morphology changes alter cryogenic toughness relative to eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The proposed mechanism is valid primarily for small Al adjustments near the eutectic composition and may fail when processing variables dominate phase evolution.
